exercise_name: Another Day In Paradise · Listening & Vocabulary
description: 《Another Day in Paradise》描寫社會中無家可歸者所面對的貧困、孤獨與冷漠，呼籲人們關注弱勢群體的處境。歌中的女子在寒冷的街頭向路人求助，卻遭到漠視，對方甚至刻意避開，假裝沒有聽見她的呼喊。她雙腳受傷、疲憊不堪，仍然努力尋找容身之所，卻始終得不到理解與幫助。歌曲以「天堂」諷刺生活安穩的人對他人苦難的無動於衷，並反覆提醒人們重新思考自己的態度。最終，《Another Day in Paradise》傳達的是同理心、社會責任與人道關懷：當我們享受平凡而舒適的生活時，也應看見那些正在受苦的人，學會放下冷漠，以尊重、理解與實際行動，為有需要的人帶來希望與溫暖。

vocabulary.usage: 想吸引遠處某人的注意時使用；常接人。
options: The guide called out to the meeting because the clock was late.
The actor called out to a new name for his movie.
Maya called out to the bus driver when she saw her bag on the bus.
Our teacher called out to that the test was easy.
optionExplanations: 錯：call out to 後面通常接被呼喊的人；會議和時鐘也不會「遲到」。
錯：要說「替電影想名字」可用 chose a new name，不能用 call out to。
對：Maya 大聲呼喊公車司機，想拿回留在車上的包包。
錯：call out to 不能直接接 that 子句；可以說 called out that...。
vocabulary.explanation: 對：Maya 大聲呼喊公車司機，想拿回留在車上的包包。

vocabulary.usage: 明明不是如此，卻故意表現得像真的一樣；常用 pretend to + 動詞。
options: The reporter pretended the station at seven every morning.
My uncle pretends very loudly when he sings at family parties.
Please pretend me your ticket before entering the museum.
Leo pretended to be a famous chef, but he could not boil an egg.
optionExplanations: 錯：pretend 不是「到達」，應說 arrived at the station。
錯：pretend 不是「唱歌」，這裡應說 sings very loudly。
錯：出示票券應用 show me your ticket，不能用 pretend me。
對：Leo 假裝自己是名廚，卻連水煮蛋都不會做。
vocabulary.explanation: 對：Leo 假裝自己是名廚，卻連水煮蛋都不會做。

vocabulary.usage: 形容「人」感到不好意思；令人尷尬的事則常用 embarrassing。
options: The science test was embarrassed, so nobody knew the answers.
Nina felt embarrassed when her phone rang during the quiet play.
We embarrassed to the train because it left early.
The new library opened with an embarrassed of books.
optionExplanations: 錯：考試「令人尷尬」要用 embarrassing；若指很難，可用 difficult。
對：安靜的舞台劇中手機突然響起，Nina 覺得很尷尬。
錯：embarrassed 是形容詞，不能當「趕車」的動詞；可說 ran to the train。
錯：embarrassed 不是表示「大量」的名詞；可說 lots of books。
vocabulary.explanation: 對：安靜的舞台劇中手機突然響起，Nina 覺得很尷尬。

vocabulary.usage: 做重要或可能有風險的事之前，先仔細想清楚。
options: The dancer thought twice across the stage in ten seconds.
My aunt thinks twice every birthday, so she is now sixty.
The pilot thought twice the plane after the long flight.
Think twice before posting that angry message online.
optionExplanations: 錯：think twice 不是「跳兩次」；應說 danced across the stage twice。
錯：think twice 不是「一年過兩次生日」；應說 has two birthdays。
錯：think twice 不能表示「檢查飛機兩次」；應說 checked the plane twice。
對：生氣時發文前先三思，可能避免後悔。
vocabulary.explanation: 對：生氣時發文前先三思，可能避免後悔。

vocabulary.usage: 鞋子磨腳、長時間走路或輕微燙傷時可能出現。
options: After the long hike, Daniel found a blister on his heel.
The singer had a blister in her voice, so she sang softly.
Our computer showed a blister because the internet was slow.
The museum was closed for a blister of three hours.
optionExplanations: 對：健行後腳跟磨出了水泡，搭配自然。
錯：聲音沙啞應說 a sore throat 或 a weak voice；blister 指皮膚上的水泡。
錯：電腦網路慢不會出現皮膚水泡；可以說 an error message。
錯：blister 不能指時間長度；應說 for three hours。
vocabulary.explanation: 對：健行後腳跟磨出了水泡，搭配自然。

vocabulary.usage: 指腳或鞋子最下面的部分；注意 sole 也可表示「唯一的」。
options: The astronaut wrote the report on the sole of the moon.
There was a small stone in the sole of my running shoe.
The band played a new sole at the music festival.
A bright sole appeared in the sky after the rain.
optionExplanations: 錯：月球的表面是 surface；sole 指腳底或鞋底。
對：鞋底卡了一顆小石頭，sole 用得正確。
錯：樂團演奏的是 song，不是 sole。
錯：雨後天空出現的可能是 rainbow；sole 不是彩虹。
vocabulary.explanation: 對：鞋底卡了一顆小石頭，sole 用得正確。

vocabulary.usage: 從表情、聲音、痕跡等線索推知某件事；常用 can tell from... that...。
options: I could tell from her smile that she liked the surprise party.
We told from the airport at six and reached the hotel at seven.
The judge told from a new rule for the football game.
Tara told from her sister a funny story about a robot.
optionExplanations: 對：從她的笑容可看出她喜歡這場驚喜派對。
錯：表示從機場出發應用 left the airport；tell from 不表示出發。
錯：制定規則應說 made a new rule；tell from 不是「訂定」。
錯：告訴姊妹故事應說 told her sister a story；不需要 from。
vocabulary.explanation: 對：從她的笑容可看出她喜歡這場驚喜派對。

vocabulary.usage: 在新學校、社團、工作團隊等環境中感到被接納。
options: We fitted in the bus at five, so it arrived on time.
My phone did not fit in with the weather, so it started to rain.
At first, Eva felt shy, but she soon fit in with her new basketball team.
The artist fit in a song to the wall with blue paint.
optionExplanations: 錯：fit in 不是「預訂」或「開動」公車；可說 got on the bus。
錯：手機不會與天氣「融入群體」；這裡語意不通。
對：Eva 一開始害羞，後來融入了新的籃球隊。
錯：在牆上作畫應用 painted；fit in 不是畫畫。
vocabulary.explanation: 對：Eva 一開始害羞，後來融入了新的籃球隊。

vocabulary.usage: 可指真的向後看，也可指回想過去；look back on 表示回顧某段經歷。
options: The nurse looked back a new medicine for the patient.
When I look back on my first job, I remember how nervous I was.
The camera looked back the stars into a larger picture.
The city looked back a new bridge across the river last year.
optionExplanations: 錯：尋找藥物應說 looked for a new medicine；look back 不表示尋找。
對：回顧第一份工作，想起當時的緊張感。
錯：放大影像應用 zoomed in on；look back 不是放大。
錯：興建橋梁應說 built a new bridge；look back 不表示建造。
vocabulary.explanation: 對：回顧第一份工作，想起當時的緊張感。

vocabulary.meaning: 請某人離開；要求移往別處
vocabulary.usage: 常指警察、保全或管理人員要求某人不要停留在某個地方；語境可能涉及權力與處境。
options: The guard moved the visitors on when the museum was closing.
The editor moved the article on because it had too many spelling mistakes.
I moved on my passport before flying to Japan.
The coach moved the team on a victory after the match.
optionExplanations: 對：博物館要關門時，警衛請參觀者離開。
錯：move someone on 是要求「人」離開；修改文章應說 edited the article。
錯：護照需要檢查可說 checked my passport；move on 不表示檢查。
錯：贏球應說 led the team to a victory；此句的 move on 搭配不對。
vocabulary.explanation: 對：博物館要關門時，警衛請參觀者離開。

audioAlignment.reviewStatus: Conservative automatic line alignment. Unmatched/overlapping background lines remain bilingual without guessed timestamps; not a full manual timing certification.

advanced.title: 進階字彙
advanced.note: 依提供的核對版材料編排；保留原有教學範圍。

questions.meaning: 吹口哨；以口哨聲示意。
questions.usage: 開心時哼出旋律、引起注意，或用口哨傳遞訊號時使用。要分清楚「吹口哨」與「唱歌」、「大喊」。
options: The baker whistled the dough until it became bread.
The librarian whistled the pages into the computer.
The referee whistled loudly to start the match.
The dentist whistled my tooth to make it cleaner.
optionExplanations: 製作麵包需要揉麵團、烘烤；不是對麵團吹口哨。
把書頁輸入電腦可以說 scan the pages，不是 whistle。
裁判吹口哨示意比賽開始；此處 whistle 表示發出口哨聲。
清潔牙齒可用 clean，吹口哨並不是牙科清潔動作。
questions.explanation: 裁判吹口哨示意比賽開始；此處 whistle 表示發出口哨聲。

questions.word: Walk on (B1；此處表示繼續往前走)
questions.meaning: 繼續走；不停下腳步。
questions.usage: 遇到某事但沒有停留、繼續前進時使用。歌曲中這個動作帶有不願停下回應的意味，但片語本身不一定表示冷漠。
options: The artist walked on the portrait with a small brush.
We rested for a minute, then walked on uphill.
My sister walked on the radio to hear the news.
The chef walked on the soup to improve its taste.
optionExplanations: 用畫筆畫肖像應說 painted the portrait，不是 walked on。
休息一會兒之後又繼續上坡走，符合「繼續前進」。
想聽廣播通常要 turn on the radio，不是 walk on。
改善湯的味道可以加香料；walk on 不是烹飪方法。
questions.explanation: 休息一會兒之後又繼續上坡走，符合「繼續前進」。

questions.meaning: 無處；沒有任何地方。
questions.usage: 表示找不到可去的地方、某物無處可放，或某件事沒有可行的地點時使用。常見於 nowhere to go / nowhere to sit / nowhere to park。
options: We parked nowhere beside the museum's front door.
She bought two nowheres at the market this morning.
My brother was nowhere his jacket before the party.
Every seat was taken, so we had nowhere to sit.
optionExplanations: 既然說停在博物館門前，就已指出具體地點；不能在此用 nowhere 表示停車位置。
nowhere 不是可數商品，不能「買兩個」。
尋找外套應說 couldn't find his jacket，不能用 nowhere 代替動詞。
所有座位都有人，因此完全沒有地方可坐；nowhere to sit 很自然。
questions.explanation: 所有座位都有人，因此完全沒有地方可坐；nowhere to sit 很自然。

questions.meaning: 天堂；（比喻）令人極度幸福、舒適或美好的地方。
questions.usage: 形容某個地方或生活狀態美好得像天堂。歌曲使用這個字時有強烈反諷：不同人的生活處境可能截然不同。
questions.prompt: 哪一句正確使用「paradise」的比喻意思？
options: With warm beaches and quiet mornings, the island felt like paradise.
The mechanic used paradise to repair my old bicycle.
The cashier gave me three paradises with my change.
The coach measured paradise before the basketball game.
optionExplanations: 用 paradise 比喻海島生活非常舒適、美好。
paradise 不是修理腳踏車的工具。
paradise 在此不是收銀員找零時發給你的可數物品。
paradise 不是能用尺測量的運動數據。
questions.explanation: 用 paradise 比喻海島生活非常舒適、美好。

questions.word: Lines on someone's face (B2；意象表達)
questions.meaning: 臉上的紋路、皺紋；有時令人聯想到年歲與人生經歷。
questions.usage: 描寫年紀、外貌或歲月留下的痕跡。Lines 在這個語境不是排隊的隊伍，也不是台詞。
questions.prompt: 哪一句正確使用「lines on someone's face」？
options: The driver painted two lines on her face of the road.
The actor memorised the lines on his face for Friday.
Years of smiling had left fine lines on her face.
The singer drew lines on her face to fix the microphone.
optionExplanations: 道路標線在路面上，不是「道路的臉上」。
演員背的是 lines（台詞），不是 lines on his face（臉部紋路）。
長年微笑讓她臉上留下細紋，符合外貌描述。
在臉上畫線不能修理麥克風；這裡的動作與目標不相符。
questions.explanation: 長年微笑讓她臉上留下細紋，符合外貌描述。

questions.meaning: 很可能；大概（有相當把握，但不是百分之百確定）。
questions.usage: 有一些理由作判斷，卻不能完全肯定時使用；與 definitely（肯定地）或 possibly（有可能）語氣不同。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最自然、準確地使用「probably」？
options: The train probably definitely arrived, without any doubt.
The clouds look dark; it will probably rain soon.
The dog wore a probably collar at the weekend market.
I probably the ticket at the station yesterday afternoon.
optionExplanations: probably 表示不完全確定；和 definitely / without any doubt 連用會造成不必要的確定程度衝突。
看見烏雲，因此推測很可能會下雨，語氣自然。
probably 不能像形容詞一樣直接形容 collar；可以說 The dog probably wore a collar.
probably 是副詞，不是「買票」的動詞；可以說 I probably bought the ticket yesterday.
questions.explanation: 看見烏雲，因此推測很可能會下雨，語氣自然。

questions.word: Been there (B2；依語境可能有比喻義)
questions.meaning: 去過那裡；（引申）經歷過那種處境。
questions.usage: 表示自己能體會某個困難，因為曾經有類似經驗。注意：歌詞只寫 she's been there；結合前後文可以作經歷艱難的理解，但不是唯一可能的字面解讀。
questions.prompt: 哪一句正確使用「been there」表示「有過類似經驗」？
options: I know how scary the first day feels. I've been there.
We have been there a new phone for my father's birthday.
I've been there the cake, so please add more sugar.
My camera has been there the music at full volume.
optionExplanations: 說話的人也經歷過第一天的緊張，因此能理解對方。
購買手機應用 bought a new phone；been there 不能代替購買動作。
been there 不表示替蛋糕加糖；句子也沒有合理的經驗語境。
播放音樂可說 played the music；been there 不是音量操作。
questions.explanation: 說話的人也經歷過第一天的緊張，因此能理解對方。

structure.title: 句型研習
structure.note: 依提供的核對版材料編排；保留原有教學範圍。

questions.meaning: 向某人高聲呼喊，以引起對方注意。
questions.usage: 對方在遠處、環境嘈雜，或你急需對方注意時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: The farmer called out to his son across the field because dinner was ready.
The farmer called out to a potato because it was late for dinner.
The farmer called out to the rain to ask where his keys were.
The farmer called out to his hat, and the hat answered in English.
optionExplanations: 兒子在田的另一邊，父親大聲呼喊有清楚目的。
馬鈴薯不是能聽懂呼喊的人，情境不合理。
向雨詢問鑰匙位置不符合一般溝通情境。
帽子不會回答問題，這是刻意設計的荒謬情境。
questions.cue: “She calls out to the man on the street”
questions.example: The coach called out to the players.
questions.explanation: 兒子在田的另一邊，父親大聲呼喊有清楚目的。

questions.meaning: 詢問能力，也可禮貌請求協助。
questions.usage: 需要別人幫忙，或想知道對方能否做一件事時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: Can you give me the moon before lunch?
Can you hold this ladder while I paint the wall?
Can the painting drive us to the concert?
Can your shoes cook dinner while you sleep?
optionExplanations: 把月亮交給別人並不是現實可行的要求。
粉刷時請別人扶梯子，是清楚可行的請求。
畫作不能開車，能力與對象不相符。
鞋子不會煮飯，所問能力不合理。
questions.example: Can you open this box?
questions.explanation: 粉刷時請別人扶梯子，是清楚可行的請求。

questions.meaning: 表示沒有任何合適的地方可以做某件事。
questions.usage: 所有座位、地方或空間都不適合時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: The train is full, so we have nowhere to sit.
There is a free room for us, so we have nowhere to sleep.
I have nowhere to put the cake because there are ten free tables.
We have nowhere to swim because the pool is open and empty.
optionExplanations: 火車沒有空位，所以無處可坐。
既然已有空房間，就不是無處可睡。
已有很多空桌子，與 nowhere to put 矛盾。
游泳池開放又空曠，不支持「沒有地方游泳」。
questions.example: We have nowhere to sit.
questions.explanation: 火車沒有空位，所以無處可坐。

questions.meaning: 問是否存在一個符合需要的地方；後面可補充那地方能做甚麼。
questions.usage: 需要尋找休息、工作、見面等適合的位置時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: Is there somewhere I can sleep? My bed is free and I am already in it.
Is there somewhere we can park? We are already in an empty car park.
Is there somewhere to buy food? I have just bought everything I need here.
Is there somewhere we can sing? The hall is closed, but the music room is open.
optionExplanations: 人已躺在空著的床上，沒有找睡處的需要。
正處於空的停車場，已有可停車的地方。
已買齊所有食物，情境沒有購買需求。
大禮堂關閉，但仍需要找另一個可唱歌的地方。
questions.cue: “Is there somewhere you can tell me?”
questions.example: Is there somewhere we can rest?
questions.explanation: 大禮堂關閉，但仍需要找另一個可唱歌的地方。

questions.meaning: 繼續往前走，不停下來。
questions.usage: 想描述人在途中繼續前進時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: The hikers rested for ten minutes and then walked on towards the lake.
After the guide said stop, everyone walked on and stayed completely still.
When the road ended at a wall, the driver walked on in his car.
The children walked on, but they stayed in the same chairs all day.
optionExplanations: 休息完繼續徒步走向湖泊，語境自然。
walked on 與「完全不動」在此直接衝突。
車裡的司機在開車，不是在步行前進。
一直坐在椅上，不符合繼續步行。
questions.example: The hikers walked on after lunch.
questions.explanation: 休息完繼續徒步走向湖泊，語境自然。

questions.word: do not / does not + base verb
questions.meaning: 用一般現在式否定習慣或一般情況。
questions.usage: 描述某人通常不做某件事時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: The museum does not open on Mondays, so we visit on Tuesday.
He does not eats meat because he is a farmer.
The robot does not walks; it rolls on wheels.
My sister do not swim on cold days.
optionExplanations: 星期一不開門，所以星期二去，否定形式也正確。
does not 後須用 eat，不是 eats。
does not 後須用 walk，不是 walks。
主詞 my sister 要配 does not。
questions.example: She does not like loud music.
questions.explanation: 星期一不開門，所以星期二去，否定形式也正確。

questions.meaning: 假裝某件事是真的，實際上未必如此。
questions.usage: 演戲、玩遊戲，或有人故意裝作不知道時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: Emma pretends her shoes are sandwiches, so she eats them for lunch.
The chef pretends that the oven is off, and then says it is definitely off.
The actor pretends he is asleep, but he is speaking loudly.
Leo pretends he is a tree, so his friends play a forest game.
optionExplanations: 把鞋真的當午餐吃並不是合理的遊戲行為。
沒有顯示「裝作」與真相之間的差別。
一邊大聲說話不符合正在假裝睡著的表現。
在森林遊戲裡扮成樹，清楚表達假裝。
questions.example: She pretends she is a queen.
questions.explanation: 在森林遊戲裡扮成樹，清楚表達假裝。

questions.meaning: 表示某個動作開始發生。
questions.usage: 想特別指出動作開始的時刻時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: The band starts to music at eight.
The band started to playing after dinner.
The band started to played at six.
The band started to play when the singer came on stage.
optionExplanations: music 是名詞，應寫 start to play music。
start to 後接原形 play，不是 playing。
to 後要用原形 play，不是 played。
歌手上台後樂隊開始演奏，時序清楚。
questions.example: The baby started to laugh.
questions.explanation: 歌手上台後樂隊開始演奏，時序清楚。

questions.meaning: 表示兩件事在相同時間發生。
questions.usage: 描述一個動作進行時另一件事也正在發生。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: The girl waved as the boat left, although there was no boat and no one left.
The girl waved as the boat left the river bank.
The girl waved as the boat left, three years before she was born.
The girl waved as the boat left, but she did not move a hand.
optionExplanations: 句中提到船離開，但後面又否定有船。
船離岸的同時女孩揮手，兩件事同時進行。
女孩尚未出生，不能在那個時間揮手。
聲稱揮手又完全沒動手，互相矛盾。
questions.example: I smiled as the train arrived.
questions.explanation: 船離岸的同時女孩揮手，兩件事同時進行。

questions.meaning: 根據所見或所聞，推測某人的感受與某個動作有關。
questions.usage: 不確定別人的內心想法，只能根據表情或行為作推測時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: Mia seems pleased to win because she says she is very sad about winning.
Mia seems pleased to win because she is smiling with her prize.
The dancer seems tired to rest because he has been sleeping for two days.
The boy seems excited to get his gift, but nobody has given him one and he knows nothing about it.
optionExplanations: 她明說對獲勝很傷心，不支持高興的推測。
笑著拿獎品是看起來高興的合理線索。
「累得想休息」並非這個詞組的自然搭配與描述。
連禮物消息都不知道，難以推測是因收到禮物而興奮。
questions.example: She seems happy to see us.
questions.explanation: 笑著拿獎品是看起來高興的合理線索。

questions.meaning: 用祈使句要求、邀請或提醒別人做事。
questions.usage: 下指示、給建議或要求對方注意時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: Please to close the gate before the goats escape.
Please closes the gate before the goats escape.
Please close the gate before the goats escape.
Please closing the gate before the goats escape.
optionExplanations: 祈使句開頭不需要 to，應用 close。
祈使句不能用第三人稱形式 closes。
祈使句用原形 close，並有合理提醒目的。
這裡不能單用 closing 作祈使動詞。
questions.example: Read this sign.
questions.explanation: 祈使句用原形 close，並有合理提醒目的。

questions.meaning: 用後面的原因解釋前面的情況。
questions.usage: 說明決定、結果或感受的原因時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: I drank three glasses of water because I wanted to be more thirsty.
I put on my warmest coat because I wanted to cool down in the sun.
I wore sunglasses because I wanted the room to become dark.
We moved the party inside because the wind was very strong.
optionExplanations: 喝水通常是解渴，不會使人更口渴。
穿最暖的外套與在太陽下想降溫互相衝突。
戴太陽眼鏡不會令整個房間變暗。
風太大，所以把派對移到室內，因果合理。
questions.example: I stayed inside because it was cold.
questions.explanation: 風太大，所以把派對移到室內，因果合理。

questions.meaning: 表示額外一個或另一個同類事物。
questions.usage: 需要再多一件物品、再一次機會或多一天時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: She bought another many tickets for the show.
We need another chairs for the guests.
I need another water because I am thirsty.
The team needs another player, because one player is ill.
optionExplanations: another 不能直接和 many tickets 連用。
another 後面通常接單數 chair，而不是 chairs。
water 不可數，這裡可說 another glass of water。
少一名隊員，所以需要另一名球員，單複數也正確。
questions.example: We need another chair.
questions.explanation: 少一名隊員，所以需要另一名球員，單複數也正確。

questions.meaning: 從眼前線索看出一件事。
questions.usage: 有可見證據，想說明自己觀察到的情況時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: I can see that the bus is here although it has not arrived and the road is empty.
I can see that the cake is ready because it is still raw inside.
I can see that the baby is sleeping because her eyes are closed and she is quiet.
I can see that the clock is broken because it tells the correct time every day.
optionExplanations: 公車未到且路上沒有車，不支持看見公車已到。
蛋糕內部仍是生的，不支持已烤好的判斷。
嬰兒閉眼又安靜，是可能正在睡覺的線索。
時鐘每天準確顯示時間，不能據此判斷故障。
questions.example: I can see that you are tired.
questions.explanation: 嬰兒閉眼又安靜，是可能正在睡覺的線索。

questions.meaning: 描述一段時間內持續發生、與現在有關的動作。
questions.usage: 想強調活動持續一段時間或現在仍可見其影響時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: They have being practising since nine.
He has been cooks all afternoon.
She has been waiting for an hour, and she is still in the line.
She has been wait for an hour, and she is still in the line.
optionExplanations: 現在完成進行式用 have been，不是 have being。
been 後須用 cooking，不是 cooks。
從一小時前等到現在，形式和時間關係都正確。
been 後要用 waiting，不是 wait。
questions.example: They have been working all morning.
questions.explanation: 從一小時前等到現在，形式和時間關係都正確。

questions.meaning: 在口語中表示擁有某物或處於某種狀況。
questions.usage: 談物品、身體狀況或已有的東西時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: The shop has got three doors, so we can enter from the front.
The shop has got to three doors, so we can enter.
The shop has got three door, so we can enter.
The shop have got three doors, so we can enter.
optionExplanations: has got 後接名詞 three doors，表達擁有。
這裡不需要 to，加入會破壞結構。
three 後要用複數 doors。
單數 shop 應配 has got，不是 have got。
questions.example: He has got a new camera.
questions.explanation: has got 後接名詞 three doors，表達擁有。

questions.meaning: 先說限制，再說與限制形成對比的努力或結果。
questions.usage: 想表達「雖然做不到／很困難，卻仍然努力」時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: I cannot play chess, but I have never tried and refuse to learn it.
I cannot play chess, but I practise with my uncle every week.
I cannot find my hat, but it is on my head and I can see it.
I cannot open the jar, but it is already open and empty.
optionExplanations: 沒有嘗試也拒絕學，沒有呈現努力的反差。
雖然不會下棋，仍每週練習，形成合理轉折。
帽子就在頭上且看見了，不能說找不到。
罐子已開，不能拿來支持打不開的限制。
questions.example: I cannot dance well, but I keep practising.
questions.explanation: 雖然不會下棋，仍每週練習，形成合理轉折。

questions.meaning: 表示不存在符合某個條件的事物。
questions.usage: 尋找所有可能方法或表達「沒有任何選擇」時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: There is nothing he can do, so he fixes the problem in one minute.
There is nothing I can read, because the library has hundreds of books I like.
There is nothing we can cook because the kitchen has no food at all.
There is nothing I can wear because every shirt is clean and fits well.
optionExplanations: 後面立刻成功修好，與 nothing he can do 不一致。
有很多喜歡的書，與「沒有可讀之物」矛盾。
廚房完全沒食物，所以沒有可煮的東西。
所有衣服都乾淨合身，與「沒衣服穿」矛盾。
questions.cue: “Is there nothing more anybody can do?”
questions.example: There is nothing I can eat.
questions.explanation: 廚房完全沒食物，所以沒有可煮的東西。

questions.meaning: 強烈相信某種事物或方法一定存在。
questions.usage: 面對困難仍相信有辦法或有答案時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: There must be another door because this room has only one door and every wall is solid.
There must be a way out, so we should look for another exit.
There must be a key somewhere; we have checked nothing yet.
There must be a bus today, although the bus company says it closed the route forever.
optionExplanations: 所有牆壁都是實心且只有一扇門，沒有支持另有門的線索。
相信仍有出口，於是主張繼續尋找，語意自然。
完全沒檢查前可猜想，但沒有明確線索支持強烈推斷。
路線已永久停運，斷言今天一定有公車缺乏依據。
questions.cue: “There must be something you can say”
questions.example: There must be a way we can help.
questions.explanation: 相信仍有出口，於是主張繼續尋找，語意自然。

questions.meaning: 根據某個線索推斷或辨認事情。
questions.usage: 從聲音、表情、痕跡或其他證據作判斷時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: You can tell from the music that the window is square.
You can tell from the wet ground that it rained recently.
You can tell from the number eight that my rabbit is a doctor.
You can tell from my sandwich that tomorrow is Friday.
optionExplanations: 音樂無法直接證明窗戶的形狀。
地面濕了是最近下過雨的合理線索。
數字八不能證明兔子的職業。
三明治不能提供明天星期幾的可靠證據。
questions.cue: “You can tell from the lines on her face”
questions.example: You can tell from the smoke that the food is burning.
questions.explanation: 地面濕了是最近下過雨的合理線索。

questions.meaning: 根據線索作強烈推測，而不只是命令。
questions.usage: 看到明顯證據，相信某種判斷很可能正確時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: The lights are off, and the cafe is locked. It must be closed.
The cake is cold and hard, so it must be fresh from the oven right now.
The lights are on and many people are eating. The cafe must be closed.
The children are asleep, so they must be running across the playground now.
optionExplanations: 鎖門加關燈是咖啡店已關門的強線索。
又冷又硬的蛋糕，不支持剛出爐的推斷。
有客人正用餐，不支持已關門的推斷。
已睡著與此刻在操場跑步互相衝突。
questions.cue: “There must be something you can say”
questions.example: You must be tired after the long trip.
questions.explanation: 鎖門加關燈是咖啡店已關門的強線索。

questions.meaning: 表示「可能已經被……」：probably 加入不確定性，被動語態強調承受動作的人。
questions.usage: 未能肯定發生了甚麼，只能推測某人過去曾被如何對待時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: The gate has probably be opened after lunch.
The gate probably been open by the guard.
The gate has probably been opening by the wind yesterday.
The gate has probably been opened because it is now open and nobody saw who did it.
optionExplanations: has 後要用 been opened，不是 be opened。
標準完整句少了 has，且被動需用 opened。
被動完成式不能用 been opening by。
門已開、沒人看見誰開的，可合理推測曾被打開。
questions.cue: “Probably been moved on from every place”
questions.example: She has probably been asked to leave.
questions.explanation: 門已開、沒人看見誰開的，可合理推測曾被打開。

questions.word: past simple negative: did not + verb
questions.meaning: 說明過去某件事沒有發生。
questions.usage: 回顧昨天、上週或更早的情況時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: My cat did not slept under the table.
We did not go to the market yesterday because it was closed.
He did not came to the show yesterday.
They did not played football last week.
optionExplanations: did not 後用 sleep，不是 slept。
昨天市場關閉，所以沒去，否定形式正確。
did not 後用 come，不是 came。
did not 後用 play，不是 played。
questions.example: They did not join the game.
questions.explanation: 昨天市場關閉，所以沒去，否定形式正確。

questions.meaning: 與某個群體或環境相處融洽、感到被接納。
questions.usage: 加入新團隊、課外活動或新社區時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: The singer fits in with the band because they refuse to speak to her and never let her sing.
The music fits in with the team because it scored three goals.
The new singer fits in with the band; they enjoy playing music together.
The table fits in at the club because it enjoys talking to people.
optionExplanations: 被全體排斥，與融入的意義相反。
音樂不能像隊員一樣射門得分。
樂隊成員相處好且享受一起演出，表示融入。
桌子不會像人一樣與會員交談融入。
questions.example: She fits in at her new club.
questions.explanation: 樂隊成員相處好且享受一起演出，表示融入。

questions.meaning: 強調某件事「不過是……」；有時會淡化事情的重要性。
questions.usage: 想描述事情很普通，或表達「只是如此」時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: It is just a small problem, so the house has completely disappeared.
It is just a small scratch, so the whole bicycle is now missing.
It is just a small scratch, so the bike still works well.
It is just a short walk, but it takes five days without stopping.
optionExplanations: 房屋完全消失不是一般能稱為小問題的情況。
整架單車不見並非小刮痕可解釋的結果。
只有小刮痕且單車仍可用，符合 just 的輕描淡寫。
不停走五天並非合理的短距離步行。
questions.example: It is just a small mistake.
questions.explanation: 只有小刮痕且單車仍可用，符合 just 的輕描淡寫。

questions.meaning: 介系詞片語補充人物或動作所在的位置。
questions.usage: 想說明事情發生於街道、房間或特定地點時。
questions.prompt: 哪一句最符合以上句型的功能和情境？
options: The fish lives in the river, so we see it swimming in the water.
The fish lives at Wednesday, so we see it in a calendar.
The fish lives in tomorrow, so we can visit it yesterday.
The fish lives on happy, so it sings in the river.
optionExplanations: 魚住在河裡，in the river 合理指出地點。
Wednesday 是時間，不是可居住的地點。
tomorrow 是時間概念，不能當魚的住所。
happy 不是這裡可用的地點名詞。
questions.example: The artist is in the garden.
questions.explanation: 魚住在河裡，in the river 合理指出地點。
